messages:
oliver: quick sync — noticed repeated short bursts of page faults during large-chat workloads, causing tail latency spikes. wondering if we should do a smoothing layer + smarter prefetch budget instead of pure immediate prefetching.

maria: saw that too. bursts usually happen after a long idle or after a long context switch (chat history). fault rate goes from ~50/s to 800/s for a few hundred ms.

raja: are these faults actual GPU page-ins or host staging faults? numbers in traces look like host->gpu DMA warms.

oliver: mostly host staging (mmapped host pages copied up). kernel time shows lots of small memcpy ops and tiny kernel launches. that kills throughput due to fill/drain.

sasha: quick thought: smoothing could introduce a short delay to coalesce nearby faults into one prefetch job. basically a debounce window. reduces number of small transfers.

liam: debounce helps but increases p90 if we wait too long. tradeoff between more tokens prefetched vs latency. want paramizable window.

maria: propose adaptive window based on recent inter-fault interval distribution + current latency SLO headroom. if headroom small -> shorter window, else coalesce more.

raja: also need fair budget per-tenant. greedy prefetch from one tenant can starve others. suggest token-buckets per-tenant and a global prefetch pool.

oliver: agree on tenant buckets. we should also limit prefetch size by model segment boundary to avoid prefetching entire 100MB segment for a 1-token need.

sasha: rough config prototype: 
```
page_fault_smoothing:
  enabled: true
  base_window_ms: 50
  max_window_ms: 300
  tenant_prefetch_budget_tokens: 1024
  global_prefetch_pool_mb: 1024
  segment_prefetch_limit_mb: 8
```

maria: thanks, looks good. segment_prefetch_limit is key. maybe add a per-request hint API so runtime can say "likely next k tokens" for better prefetch coverage.

liam: question: how does this interact with batching? prefetching too aggressively could fill the kernel queue and block smaller low-latency requests.

raja: we can integrate with the scheduler: prefetch work gets lower priority than active batch dispatch. treat prefetch as background IO with throttles.

oliver: another subtlety: prefetched KV cache pages still occupy GPU memory and may increase eviction churn. need eviction-aware prefetch: score pages by hotness and likelihood-of-reuse.

maria: that suggests tying prefetch to the quality-of-service estimate for the request (high QOS -> more aggressive prefetch). we have existing hot-score pipelines we can reuse.

sasha: telemetry plan: emit metrics: prefetch.requests, prefetch.bytes, prefetch.aborts_due_to_eviction, smoothing.coalesced_count, smoothing.window_ms. add tags tenant/model.

liam: experiment idea: AB test smoothing vs immediate prefetch; measure p50/p95/p99 latency, cost tokens, eviction churn. run on 10% of canary pool.

deploy-bot: rolled out canary flag page-fault-smoothing.v1 to 3 nodes in us-west-2 at 2833332120.

raja: implementation plan:
- small smoothing queue in runtime (coalescing window)
- tenant token-buckets + global pool enforcement
- scheduler priority for prefetch IO
- eviction-aware scoring hook for prefetch candidate pages
- telemetry + experiment flags

maria: on the scoring hook, we should avoid heavy compute on the fast path. make it an approximate score from last-k access counters.

oliver: rollout plan: dev test -> canary 10% -> rollout with kill-switch. add opt-out header for latency-critical customers.

sasha: docs: short explainer + config example, and a note about "probabilistic prefetch" for very large segments to avoid overfetch.

liam: open question: should smoothing be timeframe-based or event-count-based? timeframe seems simpler; event-count (coalesce up to N faults) might be better for very bursty but super-short storms.

raja: why not both? coalesce until time T or count N whichever first. N defaults to 8.

maria: boundary API: runtime exposes prefetch_hint(request_id, next_token_count) and prefetch_cancel(request_id) for early abort on cancellation. simple to add.

oliver: action items:
- raja: prototype smoothing queue + tenant buckets (next 2w)
- sasha: telemetry metrics + dashboard mockups (this week)
- liam: design AB test and success criteria (p50/p95/p99, eviction rate)
- maria: write short RFC draft with config proposal + opt-out hooks (by EOD Fri)

sasha: tagging product/ops in RFC for cost/ops concerns.

liam: +1 on RFC. we should include cost model numbers for prefetch bytes vs saved kernel invocations.

oliver: cool. if nobody objects I'll create the RFC repo draft and assign the action items. thanks. :thumbsup:

maria: no objections. thanks everyone.

raja: quick note: keep the smoothing window bounded small for high-concurrency tenants to avoid accumulating backlog.

deploy-bot: canary flag page-fault-smoothing.v1 removed from node i-0bcd1234 at 2833332180 (auto).
